body.en: The EST I Mathematics section tests core algebraic reasoning, problem-solving, and quantitative analysis in two parts — one without a calculator and one with. It is the primary university-admissions standardised test for international and American-diploma students across the Middle East.

label.en: ● Deep Conceptual Intuition — Test format & strategy

body.en: Proportional Invariance, Linear Structure & Quantitative Modeling: Across Egyptian Scholastic Test (EST I — Literacy & Math), multi-step problems reduce to identifying invariant quantities—constant rates of change \(m = \dfrac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}\), conservation of total work/mass, or linear system rank conditions. A two-variable linear system \(a_1 x + b_1 y = c_1\), \(a_2 x + b_2 y = c_2\) has a unique intersection if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} \ne \dfrac{b_1}{b_2}\), no solution (parallel lines) if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{b_1}{b_2} \ne \dfrac{c_1}{c_2}\), and infinitely many solutions if all three ratios coincide.

body.en: The EST I Math test runs for 90 minutes across two sections: Section I (30 min, no calculator — focuses on algebra and number sense) and Section II (60 min, calculator permitted — broader topics). The test contains 45 multiple-choice questions and 13 short constructed-response items.

label.en: ⏱ EST I Math Section Pacing & Calculator Strategy

body.en:
• Section I (No-Calculator): 20 questions in 25 minutes = 75 seconds per question. Prioritize quick mental factoring, linear equation isolation, and slope formulas. Bank easy questions in under 45 seconds to leave buffer time for the final grid-in items.
  • Section II (Calculator Permitted): 38 questions in 55 minutes = ~87 seconds per question. Use your calculator strategically to verify quadratic solutions, percentage chains, and complex statistical summaries. Never waste time typing arithmetic you can compute mentally.
  • Zero Guessing Penalty: Since there is no negative marking, never leave any question blank. With 60 seconds left, fill in answers for all remaining blank items.

label.en: ▲ The 4 Core Commandments for Scoring 750+ on EST I Math

body.en:
• 1. Linear Systems by Ratio Inspection: For the system \(a_1x + b_1y = c_1\) and \(a_2x + b_2y = c_2\): if \(\frac{a_1}{a_2} = \frac{b_1}{b_2} \neq \frac{c_1}{c_2}\), the lines are parallel (no solution). If all three ratios are equal, they are coincident (infinitely many solutions).
  • 2. Quadratic Discriminant Check: Before applying the full quadratic formula or attempting complex factoring, compute \(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac\). If \(\Delta < 0\), there are no real roots; if \(\Delta = 0\), one repeated rational root; if \(\Delta > 0\) and a perfect square, rational roots exist.
  • 3. Percentage Change Denominator Rule: Percentage change is always calculated as \(\frac{\text{new} - \text{old}}{\text{old}} \times 100\%\). Never divide by the new value! A 25% increase followed by a 20% decrease returns to the original value: \(1.25 \times 0.80 = 1.00\).
  • 4. Angle Mode & Circle Geometry: Verify whether angles are in radians or degrees. Remember that arc length \(s = r\theta\) (where \(\theta\) is in radians) and sector area \(A = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta\). In degrees, \(s = \frac{\theta}{360} 2\pi r\) and \(A = \frac{\theta}{360} \pi r^2\).

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Test format & strategy)

body.en:
Why Successive Multipliers & Harmonic Average Speed Work: If a quantity \(Q_0\) undergoes a percentage change \(p\%\) followed by \(q\%\), the compound multiplier is the product of individual scale factors:

\[ Q_{\text{final}} = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\!\left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right) = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p + q}{100} + \frac{pq}{10000}\right) \]

Notice the cross term \(\dfrac{pq}{10000}\): an increase of \(p\%\) followed by a decrease of \(p\%\) yields \(Q_0\bigl(1 - (p/100)^2\bigr) < Q_0\). Similarly, traveling equal distance \(d\) at speeds \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) takes total time \(T = \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2}\), so average speed is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \dfrac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

label.en: Worked Example A — Test format & strategy (Medium Application)

body.en:
Problem (Medium): For all positive values of \( x \), which expression is equivalent to \( x^{\frac{4}{5}} \)?

Step-by-Step Solution: By the definition of rational exponents: \[ x^{\frac{m}{n}} = \sqrt[n]{x^m} = (\sqrt[n]{x})^m \] where \( n \) is the index of the radical (root) and \( m \) is the power. Thus, \( x^{\frac{4}{5}} = \sqrt[{5}]{x^{4}} \). Final Answer: \( \sqrt[{5}]{x^{4}} \).

label.en: Worked Example B — Test format & strategy (Hard Application)

body.en:
Problem (Hard): Consider the factored quartic polynomial \( f(x) = (x^2 - 121)(x^2 - 289) \). What is the constant term \( f(0) \)?

Step-by-Step Solution: Evaluating at \( x = 0 \) gives \( f(0) = (-121)(-289) = 34969 \).

label.en: Worked Example C — Test format & strategy (Easy Application)

body.en:
Problem (Easy): The linear system \( 20x + 25y = 535 \) and \( 40x + (f + 25)y = 1075 \) has no solution. What is the constant parameter \( f \)?

Step-by-Step Solution: A linear system has no solution when the lines are parallel and distinct: \( \frac{40}{20} = \frac{f + 25}{25} \implies f = 25 \).

label.en: Worked Example D — Test format & strategy (Easy Application)

body.en:
Problem (Easy): What are the solutions to the quadratic equation \( x^2 - 4x - 3 = 0 \)?

Step-by-Step Solution: Apply the quadratic formula \( x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} \) where \( a = 1 \), \( b = -4 \), and \( c = -3 \): \[ x = \frac{-(-4) \pm \sqrt{(-4)^2 - 4(1)(-3)}}{2(1)} \] \[ x = \frac{4 \pm \sqrt{16 - -12}}{2} = \frac{4 \pm \sqrt{28}}{2} \] \[ x = \frac{4 \pm 2\sqrt{7}}{2} = 2 \pm \sqrt{7} \]. Final Answer: \( 2 \pm \sqrt{7} \).

question.en: Section I of EST I Math contains 20 questions in 25 minutes. If a student answers the first 12 questions in an average of 50 seconds each, how many seconds per question are available for the remaining 8 questions?

solution.en: \(\text{Time for first 12 questions} = 12 \times 50 = 600\text{ seconds}\) (10 minutes). \(\text{Total time} = 25 \times 60 = 1500\text{ seconds}\). \(\text{Remaining time} = 1500 - 600 = 900\text{ seconds}\). For the remaining 8 questions: \(\frac{900}{8} = 112.5\text{ seconds per question}\) (1 minute 52.5 seconds per question).

question.en: [Practice 4 · Medium] Which ordered pair \( (x, y) \) satisfies the system of inequalities below? \[ \begin{aligned} y &> 3x + 1 \\ y &\le -x + 10 \end{aligned} \]

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Test format & strategy and start from \( (x, y) \).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \((1, 6)\).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

solution.en:
Test the ordered pair \((1, 6)\) in both inequalities:
1) \(6 > 3(1) + 1 = 4\), which is \(6 > 4\) (True).
2) \(6 \le -(1) + 10 = 9\), which is \(6 \le 9\) (True).
Both conditions are satisfied.
